facts.detail: BDUK, as a DSIT executive agency, commissioned the Project Gigabit evaluation.
Ipsos UK and partners were commissioned to undertake the work.
The evaluation covers Gigabit Infrastructure Subsidy and Gigabit Broadband Voucher interventions.
The plan evaluates increased access to gigabit networks for non-commercial premises.
The plan includes questions about changes in available speeds and prices.
The evaluation considers interactions between GIS, GBVS and GigaHub interventions.
It considers spill-over, crowding-out and crowding-in effects.
As of autumn 2024 the plan cited 36 awarded contracts, 15 in procurement and at least five still to procure.
A 2025 baselining exercise was recommended using secondary data for 2020.
The plan proposes an interim evaluation in 2028 and a final evaluation in 2032 or after contract completion.

facts.detail: The GigaHub Process Review annex was published on 26 June 2026.
The annex was authored by Belmana.
The study was conducted by Belmana and GC Insight.
Belmana acted as an independent contractor for BDUK.
The annex provides technical detail supporting the main process-review findings.
GigaHubs are gigabit-capable connections for remote public buildings.
Examples include schools, GP surgeries and libraries.
The Hubs were delivered as part of Project Gigabit.
The annex documents modelling assumptions.
It documents scoping patterns and the qualitative evidence-gathering approach.

facts.detail: The GigaHubs Process Review Summary was published on 26 June 2026.
Belmana authored the summary.
Belmana and GC Insight conducted the study.
The summary describes BDUK's Hub product.
The Hub product mobilises resources to secure gigabit-capable connections.
The target locations are remote public buildings.
Schools are included among target buildings.
GP surgeries are included among target buildings.
Libraries are included among target buildings.
The expansion of Gigabit Infrastructure Subsidy shaped GigaHubs delivery.
